lockFileMaintenance.description: Renovate only bumps the direct dependencies in pyproject.toml. Refreshing poetry.lock weekly keeps the transitive ones (urllib3, certifi, lxml, ...) current as well. A lock refresh has no release date, so with the default timestamp-required its minimum-release-age check would stay pending forever and it would never automerge. The 7 days still apply to what it locks: Renovate runs Poetry with POETRY_SOLVER_MIN_RELEASE_AGE taken from minimumReleaseAge

packageRules.description: Safely automerge patch and digest updates

Python updates: create the branch only once the release is older than minimumReleaseAge. Renovate's default creates it at once with a pending check, but it runs Poetry with the same minimum age, so Poetry refuses to lock the release and the branch fails CI until it is retried after the wait

poetry-core under [build-system]: with package-mode = false nothing is ever built, so its version does not matter, and Poetry refuses to lock it ('not dependencies of this project'), which fails every update branch that touches it
